This petition is filed by sole accused under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. seeking bail in Crime No.81/2022 of Tavaregera Police Station for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 376 of IPC and Section 4 and 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act).

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The case of the prosecution is that respondent No.2 filed complaint stating that the victim girl who is her daughter aged 14 years went out of the house on 21.07.2022 at about 7.30 p.m. to bring notes from her friend's house and did not return and they searched for her and she was not traced and accused Vijay Kumar who was visiting their house along with her son Vinod Kumar, she filed complaint which came to be registered in crime No.81/2022 for the offence U/s 363 I.P.C against the petitioner.
3. The petitioner came to be arrested on 28.07.2022.
The charge sheet came to be filed against the petitioners for the offence under Section 363,376 and Section 4 and 6 of POCSO Act, 2012.
4. The appellant who is in judicial custody has filed bail application in Special SC.POCSO No.52/2022 and the same came to be rejected by order dated 23.12.2022.
Therefore, the petitioner is before this Court seeking bail.

5. Heard the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent No.1-State.
6.
Respondent No.2 inspite of service of notice remained absent and unrepresented.

entities.text: Sri Vijaykumar Chawan vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that on perusal of the statement of the victim girl along with her further statement, it is clear that she was in love affair with petitioner and she voluntarily went along with him.
The victim girl is aged 14 years and she is aware of consequences of her acts.
The statement of CWs.6 and 7 reveals that they saw the petitioner along with victim girl in temple on 23.07.2022 and 24.07.2022.
There are contradictions in the statement of victim girl recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and statement recorded by the police.
The charge sheet is filed and the petitioner is not required for custodial interrogation.
With this, he prayed to allow the petition.
8. Per contra, learned HCGP for respondent No.1- State would contend that the date of birth of the victim girl is 11.06.2008 as per her school records and she is aged 14 years.
The statement of the victim girl recorded by the police and the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. reveals that the petitioner enticed her and had sexual intercourse.
The doctor who has examined the victim girl has opined that her hymen is ruptured.
The charge sheet material shows prima-facie case against the petitioner for the offences alleged against him.
He further submits that CWs.10 to 12 are eyewitnesses who have seen the victim girl with this petitioner when they were secured by the police.
With this, he prayed to reject the petition.
9. Having heard the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned HCGP for respondent No.1-State, this Court has gone through the charge sheet records.
10. The date of birth of victim girl is 11.6.2008 as per her school records.
The victim girl is aged 14 years as on the date of alleged offence.
On perusal of the statement of victim girl recorded by the police reveals that she was in love affair with this petitioner and she went with him on his motorcycle and stayed in Durgadevi temple.
There is no allegation of forcible sexual intercourse on the victim girl and the victim girl had stayed with this petitioner from 21.07.2022 to 28.07.2022.
The victim girl is of the age of understanding the consequences of her acts.
As the charge sheet is filed, the petitioner is not required for custodial interrogation.
11. The petitioner is aged 21 years and if he is not granted bail, will come in contact with hard core criminals.
The main objection of the prosecution is that there is threat to the complainant and other prosecution witnesses which can be met with by imposing some stringent conditions.
12. This Court is of the view that there are grounds for granting bail to the petitioner by imposing stringent conditions.

13. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
The impugned order dated 23.12.2022 passed in Special S.C.POCSO No.52/2022 by the Addl. District and Sessions Judge FTSC-I, Koppal is set aside.
